details:
Seed to satellite

Seed to satellite is a web-based tool that helps farmers compare different crop rotation plans and understand how climate conditions may affect their choices. The idea behind our project is simple: farmers should not only consider the weather today, but also learn from past weather conditions before planning their next growing seasons.

Our platform uses historical climate data from NASA POWER covering the period from 2005 to 2024. Users can select an agricultural location, choose from seven available crops, and set their priorities, such as saving water, improving soil health, increasing potential returns, and reducing agricultural risks.

Based on these choices, the platform generates three possible crop rotation plans. Each plan receives an evaluation score out of 100, along with an explanation to help users understand the results and compare the available options. it also allows users to explore different climate scenarios by changing temperature and water availability. In addition, we included a case study based on the August 2015 heat wave in the Nile Delta to demonstrate how challenging weather conditions can be considered during agricultural planning.

We used NASA POWER for climate data, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to build the application, and GitHub Pages to make it publicly accessible.

What makes our project different is that it connects historical climate information with practical crop rotation choices. Instead of simply showing weather data, it gives users a way to explore different agricultural plans and understand their possible performance under changing conditions.

Our main goal is to make climate information easier to use in agriculture and help farmers make more informed decisions. We hope seed to satellite can encourage better water management, crop diversity, and more climate-aware farming practices.

During development, we considered several factors, including location, crop availability, planting seasons, temperature, precipitation, water availability, soil health, potential returns, and agricultural risks. We also focused on keeping the platform simple and accessible for users without a technical background.
